manifest.name: dsh-github-panel
manifest.description: GitHub account panel for the DeepSeek Harness Web UI: sign in through the GitHub CLI, browse your contribution dashboard, and let the agent push with that account.
manifest.author: Ayleovelle

readme.text:
English | [中文](README.zh.md)

A GitHub panel for the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) Web UI.

It adds a GitHub entry to the left sidebar. Open it to see the signed-in GitHub account, a
contribution heatmap for the past year, commit / pull-request / issue / review totals, streaks,
follower and repository counts, and the most recently active repositories. The plugin also gives
the agent a `github_push` tool so pushes to GitHub use the same account.

Sign-in is the **GitHub CLI's official OAuth device flow**: there is no OAuth App to register and
no Client ID or Client Secret to paste. An existing `gh` login is reused as-is; when `gh` is logged
out, one click opens the official GitHub login (a terminal window plus the browser) and the panel
refreshes itself afterwards.

- **Sidebar panel** — a GitHub icon in the left sidebar opens a full-width page in the main column.
- **Zero-setup sign-in** — reuses the local GitHub CLI account; no app registration, no secrets in
  configuration.
- **Contribution dashboard** — last-year contribution heatmap, total contributions, current and
  longest streaks, commits / PRs / issues / reviews, private contributions, followers / following /
  repositories, and the 10 most recently pushed repositories.
- **Organization view** — every organization you belong to is listed with its member and repository
  count; click one to see its members, teams, recent repositories, and your own contributions in it.
  A separate card splits your yearly contributions (commits / PRs / issues) by owning account, so
  personal and organization work are comparable at a glance.
- **`github_push` agent tool** — pushes a local Git branch with `gh auth git-credential`, so the
  token never appears in command-line arguments or environment values, and sets the repository's
  local commit identity to the signed-in account
  (`<id>+<login>@users.noreply.github.com`).
- **Prompt guidance** — the Host half registers a short system-prompt section

- DeepSeek Harness with the Web UI (this is a Web client plugin plus a Host plugin).
- [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com/) (`gh`) installed and signed in once
  (`gh auth login`). The plugin discovers `gh` on `PATH`, in its `bin` subdirectories, and in the
  usual install locations.

Install the bundle from GitHub with Plugin Manager (sidebar **Plugins** → add a plugin) using:

```text
github:Ayleovelle/dsh-github-panel
```

Alternatively point Plugin Manager's installation at the absolute directory of a local checkout; it
links the directory and enables the bundle. Restart DSH if your composition does not apply bundles
live.

1. Open the DSH Web UI and click the GitHub icon in the left sidebar.
2. If `gh` is already signed in (check with `gh auth status`), the panel shows that account's
   dashboard immediately.
3. Otherwise press **Open GitHub login**: the official login opens (a terminal window plus the
   browser), and the panel refreshes when the authorization completes.
4. Ask the agent to push a branch to GitHub. It calls `github_push`, which authenticates through
   the GitHub CLI and signs commits with the same account.
To use another account, run `gh auth switch` in a terminal and refresh the panel.

- **Host half** (`index.js`): locates and calls `gh`, fetches the viewer dashboard through
  `gh api graphql` (the token stays inside the GitHub CLI), serves a small same-origin JSON bridge
  at `/dsh-github/*`, registers the `github_push` tool, and adds one system-prompt section.
- **Client half** (`client.js`): a plain browser module that registers the sidebar icon
  (`sidebar.panellist`, id `github`) and the main panel (`main`, key `github`), then renders the
  dashboard with React. UI text is localized in English and Chinese.
- **Panel bridge**: loopback-only (`127.0.0.1` / `localhost` / `::1`), POST requests require a
  custom header (cross-site requests fail the CORS preflight), no token is ever returned to the
  browser, and no `/api` authentication is used. Endpoints: `status`, `dashboard`,
  `organization?login=`, and `login`.
- **Push authentication**: `git -c credential.helper= -c credential.helper='!gh auth git-credential' push`,
  with the GitHub CLI's directory prepended to `PATH` for the child process.

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `DSH_GH_PATH` (or `GH_PATH`) | Absolute path to the `gh` executable when it cannot be discovered automatically. |

The plugin is plain ES modules — no build step, no dependencies in this package:

```text
index.js          Host half: GitHub CLI discovery, gh api calls, HTTP bridge, github_push tool
client.js         Client half: sidebar icon + main panel (plain browser module, React from the host)
cordis.patch.yml  Bundle patch inserting the `github-panel` row
locale/en.json    Plugin Manager title and description

Install the checkout with Plugin Manager (local directory target) and edit the files; a profile
recomposition reloads changed code. The panel bridge can be checked directly while DSH is running:

```powershell
Invoke-WebRequest http://127.0.0.1:<port>/dsh-github/status
Invoke-WebRequest http://127.0.0.1:<port>/dsh-github/dashboard
Invoke-WebRequest "http://127.0.0.1:<port>/dsh-github/organization?login=<org>"
```

- No GitHub token is read, stored, or transmitted by this plugin. `gh` owns the credential and
  injects it into git through its credential helper.
- The local JSON bridge refuses non-loopback `Host` headers and cross-site `Origin`s, and the
  panel never displays a token.
- Revoke access with `gh auth logout` or from GitHub's authorized OAuth apps settings.
